clue.text: Shot a drug? It was smoked, in fact, in Wonderland

definitions.text: It was smoked, in fact, in Wonderland

parts.note: a hook is a shot in golf or cricket that curves away
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a drug was taken, then recalls the Caterpillar puffing away in Alice's Wonderland.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the Caterpillar sits on a mushroom smoking a water pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caterpillar in Carroll's story smokes a water pipe of this kind.

clue.text: Herb, mainly a captain's servant in a picaresque novel

definitions.text: a captain's servant in a picaresque novel

indicators.note: mainly asks for most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: oregano is a culinary herb, also called wild marjoram

explanation.surface: A recipe herb seems to belong to a seafaring officer's manservant in a rambling eighteenth-century tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a minor character, a servant to a ship's captain, in a picaresque story of adventure.

clue.text: A Wilde book about a poor boy

definitions.meaning: ... Wilde is an English pop singer of the 1980s
Kipling's novel follows an orphaned Irish boy living on the streets of Lahore

explanation.surface: Someone describes an Oscar Wilde work about a destitute lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilde' points to Oscar, but it is the singer Kim Wilde; the poor boy is the orphan hero of Kipling's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's novel is named after its orphan hero, and the same first name belongs to the singer surnamed Wilde.

clue.text: Worshipper seen in church in dungarees

indicators.note: seen in says the letters can be spotted running through the following words

explanation.surface: A worshipper turns up at church wearing dungarees.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Indian religion that worships gods such as Vishnu and Shiva.

clue.text: Bristle with arrogance or reserve

parts.note: a seta is a bristle or stiff hair in zoology
side is old slang for a pretentious, haughty manner

explanation.surface: Someone bristles with haughtiness or holds back coolly.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to put it by for later use.

clue.text: Pinter's play that has no words?

definitions.meaning: Harold Pinter wrote a short 1969 play of this name
a state with nothing spoken at all

explanation.surface: A Pinter play, famous for its pauses, is imagined as containing no dialogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinter is known for long pauses, which makes the second reading feel like a joke about his style.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinter's 1969 play carries the name, and a total absence of speech is exactly that quiet.

clue.text: Herrick wrote this book, about one in Hamlet maybe

indicators.note: about says the book's letters go round the rest

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the word for Hamlet

parts.note: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, so an example of a Dane
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Herrick wrote a volume concerning a character in Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Herrick, the seventeenth-century poet, addressed several lyrics to women by name, this among them.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a short lyric by the poet Robert Herrick addressed to a woman.

clue.text: Courteous knight shook up about dodgy CID liar

indicators.note: about says the sore letters wrap around the shuffled ones

parts.note: someone shaken up is upset or sore

indicators.note: dodgy suggests something unreliable, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gallant knight is rattled by a shady detective who lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shook up' looks like the anagram signal, but it means upset; 'dodgy' does the shuffling. CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spenser's Faerie Queene, Book VI follows this knight, the champion of courtesy.

clue.text: Heresy in church? It is embraced by friar.

indicators.note: embraced by says the following letters sit inside the title for a friar

parts.note: Dom is the title given to certain monks and friars
CE is the Church of England
'tis is the old contraction of it is

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a heresy lurks in church and is told that a friar holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: An early Christian heresy holding that Christ only seemed to have a physical body.

clue.text: Novel in which revolutionary miner is protected by revolutionary prisoner?

indicators.note: is protected by says the shuffled letters sit inside the turned word
revolutionary means the word for prisoner turns round

parts.note: a lag is a convict, as in old lag

indicators.note: revolutionary means the letters of the word overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A novel in which a rebel miner is sheltered by a rebel convict.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'revolutionary' words do different jobs: the first shuffles, the second turns a word round. Zola's novel concerns a miners' strike, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Zola's novel about a coal miners' strike in northern France takes its name from a month of the Revolutionary calendar.

clue.text: Run through command point

definitions.meaning: to run a business or film is to manage it
a through train goes straight there without changes
to command someone is to order them
to point someone the way is to show it to them

explanation.surface: An order is given to run straight through a checkpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense matches: to manage, straight without stops, to order, and to aim or show the way.

clue.text: Devious Punch, a liar whose advice was good at least sometimes

definitions.text: whose advice was good at least sometimes

indicators.note: devious means crooked, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crooked puppet character and a liar give advice that is sometimes sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar's wife warned him not to go to the Senate on the Ides of March; Shakespeare's Folio spells her name with PH.
explanation.definitionFit: In Julius Caesar, the dictator's wife dreams of his murder and begs him to stay home, sound counsel he ignores.

clue.text: Appeal represented with irony in a sci-fi book?

indicators.note: represented read as re-presented, these letters are set out again in another form

explanation.surface: A plea is restated ironically in a science fiction novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Kurt Vonnegut's first novel, of 1952, imagines a world of automated machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurt Vonnegut's dystopian first novel takes its title from a self-playing keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Work on England that was written by Dumas père

definitions.text: that was written by Dumas père

parts.note: to act is to work or function

explanation.surface: Someone works on an English text attributed to the elder Dumas.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel by Alexandre Dumas the elder, set in Nero's Rome and named after the emperor's mistress.

clue.text: "A catholic? Begin again." Is it mostly advice for religious ladies?

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article a before a vowel
to renew something is to start it afresh
taken as written

indicators.note: mostly asks for most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A Catholic is urged to make a fresh start, and wonders whether this is guidance for nuns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SEX to SE. The work is a thirteenth-century guide for anchoresses, women who lived walled up in a cell beside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle English rule book giving guidance to anchoresses, women who withdrew from the world for prayer.

clue.text: Literary addict's plant, delivered and rejected, say

parts.note: cole is cabbage or a related plant
to deliver from something is to rid of it

indicators.note: rejected means the abbreviation for say is thrown back the other way

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A writer's plant is delivered to him and then refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns EG to GE. The poet of Kubla Khan was famously addicted to opium.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romantic poet of Kubla Khan was a lifelong opium user.

clue.text: Pound, a writer of verses who inspired another one

parts.note: to pound is to beat
Tim Rice wrote song lyrics for musicals such as Evita

explanation.surface: Ezra Pound, a poet, is said to have inspired another poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' suggests Ezra Pound the poet, but it is a verb. The other writer of verses is Dante, inspired by his Florentine muse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's muse was the Florentine woman Portinari, who guides him through Paradise in his poem.

clue.text: Request to hold onto one sci-fi book with many copies

definitions.meaning: a plea to keep hold of the speaker
Ishiguro's novel is about cloned children bred for organ donation, so many copies of people

explanation.surface: A plea not to be released, and a science fiction novel that sold widely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many copies' looks like a bestseller's print run but means clones.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishiguro's novel about clones takes its title from a song of that plea.

clue.text: Poem about love in a Christian movement, with Lionel oddly

parts.note: Toc H is a Christian charitable movement founded in the First World War

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the following name

explanation.surface: A love poem sits within a church movement, along with someone called Lionel.
explanation.walkthrough: Several poets, including Robert Burns, wrote love poems with this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A title used for love lyrics by several poets, addressed to a beloved woman.

clue.text: Payments going the wrong way in Post Office? That's fraudulent

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters inside the abbreviation
going the wrong way means the word for payments runs backwards

parts.note: dues are payments owed

explanation.surface: Money vanishing at the post office counter suggests fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going the wrong way' sounds like money misrouted, which suits the fraud picture, but it signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sham or pretended is false, as fraud is.

clue.text: Call that can be long in cricket and short in baseball

definitions.text: Call that can be long in cricket and short in baseball

parts.words: Call that can be long in cricket and short in baseball
parts.note: a call to halt; prefixed long it is a cricket fielding position behind the wicketkeeper, prefixed short a baseball position between second and third base

explanation.surface: A call that changes length between two bat-and-ball games.
explanation.walkthrough: Long stop in cricket stands behind the wicketkeeper; shortstop in baseball fields between second and third base.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for halting that forms both a cricket fielding position and a baseball one.

clue.text: Maybe Scheherezade's European, fat and pedestrian, going west?

indicators.note: going west in an across answer means the letters are read right to left

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
a pedestrian has no car

explanation.surface: Scheherazade is pictured as a plump European walking towards the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns E, SUET and NO CAR round to give the answer. Scheherazade tells stories night after night in the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Scheherazade is the storyteller of the Thousand and One Nights, a female teller of tales.

clue.text: Lorraine's place as someone important in a Dickens novel

definitions.meaning: the city is the historic capital of Lorraine in north-east France

definitions.text: someone important in a Dickens novel
definitions.meaning: a key character in Oliver Twist, Bill Sikes's lover

explanation.surface: A French city's importance is compared to a character in Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Lorraine, and Sikes's doomed partner in Oliver Twist bears the name.

clue.text: Shakespearean general who once had to be told about fighting

definitions.text: Shakespearean general who once had to be told about fighting

parts.words: Shakespearean general who once had to be told about fighting
parts.note: in Macbeth, the English commander leading troops against the tyrant has to be told that his son died in battle

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean general had to be briefed on a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth, the old Earl of Northumberland learns his son has died fighting Macbeth, and asks only whether the wounds were on his front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Northumberland who commands the English forces against Macbeth in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: One described as using Lance Percival's weapon holder?

definitions.text: One described as using Lance Percival's weapon holder?

parts.words: One described as using Lance Percival's weapon holder?
parts.note: Lance Percival was a British comic actor, but read as the lance of Grail legend; its holder is the Roman centurion said to have pierced Christ's side, and the same name belongs to the Greek author of a treatise on style

explanation.surface: Someone is said to use a weapon owned by the British comedian Lance Percival.
explanation.walkthrough: Lance Percival was a British comic actor; the Holy Lance appears in Grail stories of Percival, and the centurion who wielded it shares a name with the author of On the Sublime, who described literary style.
explanation.definitionFit: The centurion of legend held the spear that pierced Christ, and the name is also that of a Greek critic who wrote on style.

clue.text: One Springfield location that's seedy

definitions.meaning: Springfield is the capital of Illinois

explanation.surface: A place in Springfield is described as run down.
explanation.walkthrough: There are many Springfields; one is the state capital of Illinois.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy is informal for poorly or out of sorts, and the abbreviation names the state containing one Springfield.

clue.text: Joke in Bard's work like Romeo and Juliet

indicators.note: in places the word for joke inside the word for the Bard's work

parts.note: Shakespeare, the Bard, wrote in verse
a joke is a good one, as in 'that's a good one'

explanation.surface: A gag is found in Shakespeare's tragedy of the young lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Juliet are both from Verona, so they are natives of that city.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young lovers both come from Verona, so they are natives of that Italian city.

clue.text: Tone of 1920s novel, other than chapter on city

indicators.note: other than says the following letters are taken away from the novel's title

parts.note: Crome Yellow is Aldous Huxley's first novel, published in 1921

indicators.note: on places the chapter letter in front of the city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: Someone describes the tone of a 1920s novel apart from its chapter on a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C and ROME from Huxley's Crome Yellow and the colour is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is a colour, and tone can mean a shade or hue.
